cues.en: Instructor: Everyone makes mistakes.
cues.zh: 講師：每個人都會犯錯。

cues.en: It's a natural part of life.
cues.zh: 這是生活很自然的一部分。

cues.en: So in statistics, we also can make mistakes, we can make statistical errors.
cues.zh: 統計中也可能犯錯，產生統計錯誤。

cues.en: And there are different types of mistakes that we can make with statistical significances.
cues.zh: 判斷統計顯著性時，可能有不同類型的錯誤。

cues.en: These are called type I errors and type II errors.
cues.zh: 稱為第一類錯誤和第二類錯誤。

cues.en: And so in this video, I'm going to introduce you to these different types of errors.
cues.zh: 這部影片會介紹這些不同錯誤。

cues.en: And towards the end, I will discuss how to minimize the chances of making these errors in the first place.
cues.zh: 最後會討論，如何盡量降低一開始就犯錯的機率。

cues.en: Okay, so going back a few lectures to where we had a null hypothesis distribution and an alternative hypothesis distribution.
cues.zh: 回到幾堂前，虛無假設分布和對立假設分布的概念。

cues.en: Now, remember, the null hypothesis distribution comes from a formula.
cues.zh: 記住，虛無假設分布來自公式。

cues.en: We evaluate a formula, like a T distribution or an F distribution, and that's how we derive our null hypothesis distribution.
cues.zh: 計算某個公式，例如 t 分布、F 分布，就能得到虛無假設分布。

cues.en: The alternative hypothesis distribution is a little bit more of like a conceptual idea because in most cases, we're not actually going out in the same study
cues.zh: 對立假設分布比較像概念，因為大部分情況，同一研究中不會真的

cues.en: and drawing multiple, multiple, like hundreds and hundreds of repeated samples from the population.
cues.zh: 從母體重複抽數百個樣本。

cues.en: Typically, we only have one sample, and so we have one statistic.
cues.zh: 通常只有一個樣本，因此只有一個統計量。

cues.en: So you have one value that, you know, corresponds to your alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 有一個對應對立假設的值。

cues.en: And the question is, what is the probability that that value that you observed in your one sample actually belongs in the null hypothesis distribution,
cues.zh: 問題是，單一樣本中觀察到的值，實際屬於虛無假設分布，

cues.en: or the alternative hypothesis distribution?
cues.zh: 或對立假設分布的機率是多少？

cues.en: And then you have your significance threshold here, your alpha level here.
cues.zh: 這裡是顯著性門檻，也就是 α 水準。

cues.en: And then the idea is that if your value falls further to the right or further to the left, if it's two-tailed.
cues.zh: 概念是，如果值落在更右側，或雙尾時更左側，

cues.en: So if it's more extreme, the value that you observe in your sample data is more extreme than this threshold value under the null hypothesis,
cues.zh: 也就是比虛無假設下這個門檻更極端，

cues.en: we would call that statistically significant.
cues.zh: 就稱為統計顯著。

cues.en: But, as I've already explained before, that doesn't guarantee that the effect is real, that just says that it's unlikely given the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 但如前面解釋，這不保證效果是真的，只表示在虛無假設下不太可能。

cues.en: Okay, so looking at these two distributions and the significance threshold here gives us a table like this.
cues.zh: 觀察兩個分布和顯著性門檻，就能得到這張表。

cues.en: So this is the reality about the world whether the null hypothesis is true or the null hypothesis is false.
cues.zh: 這是真實世界的狀況：虛無假設為真，或為假。

cues.en: This is not something we can really know, we can just sort of imagine that one of these two things is real.
cues.zh: 實際上無法真正知道，只能想像其中一種是真實的。

cues.en: And then you make your decision, based on the data that you've collected, the statistic you ran, and the significance threshold.
cues.zh: 再根據收集的資料、統計量，以及顯著性門檻做決定。

cues.en: So you reject the null hypothesis in favor of the alternative hypothesis, or you don't reject the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 拒絕虛無假設、傾向對立假設，或者不拒絕虛無假設。

cues.en: You say, well, I will tentatively hold on the null hypothesis, I'm not going to reject that in favor of the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 也就是暫時保留虛無假設，不拒絕它而轉向對立假設。

cues.en: Okay, so now we can come up with two ways of being correct and two ways of making a mistake.
cues.zh: 於是有兩種正確方式，以及兩種犯錯方式。

cues.en: So we call this a true positive, this means that our sample gave us a null hypothesis, or a test statistic value,
cues.zh: 這稱為真陽性，表示樣本給出的虛無假設，或者檢定統計量，

cues.en: that was more extreme than the significance threshold.
cues.zh: 比顯著性門檻更極端。

cues.en: And it really did come from an alternative hypothesis distribution, so this is correct.
cues.zh: 它真的來自對立假設分布，所以是正確的。

cues.en: The true positive means the null hypothesis really is false and we correctly rejected it.
cues.zh: 真陽性表示，虛無假設確實為假，而我們正確拒絕它。

cues.en: So that's how things really are in the world, and this is correct.
cues.zh: 這就是真實世界的情況，而這個判斷正確。

cues.en: This is called one minus beta, beta is related to the power of your statistical test.
cues.zh: 這稱為 1−β，β 和統計檢定力有關。

cues.en: I'm gonna talk more about that in a later section of the course.
cues.zh: 課程後面會多談。

cues.en: So for now, you can just remember that this is called a true positive.
cues.zh: 目前只要記住，這叫真陽性。

cues.en: This one minus beta thing, you'll learn about this later on.
cues.zh: 1−β 的部分，之後會學。

cues.en: Okay, so then we get to this area over here.
cues.zh: 接著到這個區域。

cues.en: And this is also correct, this is a true negative.
cues.zh: 這也正確，是真陰性。

cues.en: This means that the null hypothesis is true, and we didn't reject it.
cues.zh: 表示虛無假設為真，而且沒有拒絕它。

cues.en: And, again, you know, the, the term, the wording, the phrasing gets a little confusing here because we don't really accept the null hypothesis, we just don't reject the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 用詞有點混淆，因為不是真的接受虛無假設，只是不拒絕。

cues.en: But the true state of the world is that the null hypothesis is true, and we tentatively maintain that the null hypothesis is true.
cues.zh: 但真實世界確實是虛無假設為真，我們也暫時維持這個判斷。

cues.en: So this is called a true negative.
cues.zh: 這稱為真陰性。

cues.en: And I guess, you know, that also does kind of include this area over here.
cues.zh: 我想，也包含這裡這個區域。

cues.en: But depending on how you see this perspective, I guess I was envisioning the null hypothesis distribution be behind the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 取決於如何看這個視角，大概當時想像虛無假設分布在對立假設後面。

cues.en: I don't know what I was thinking.
cues.zh: 不知道當時怎麼想的。

cues.en: Anyway, when the null hypothesis is true and the value is less than the significance threshold, you do not reject the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 總之，虛無假設為真，而且值低於顯著性門檻時，就不拒絕虛無假設。

cues.en: You say that the effect is not statistically significant, and that is the correct interpretation, that's the right thing to say.
cues.zh: 說效果沒有統計顯著性，這是正確的解讀、正確的說法。

cues.en: The effect isn't there, and you claim it isn't there.
cues.zh: 效果不存在，而你也主張不存在。

cues.en: Okay, so those are the two ways of being correct.
cues.zh: 這是兩種正確方式。

cues.en: Now, we get to the two errors.
cues.zh: 接著看兩種錯誤。

cues.en: So we can have what's called a type II error, and it's also called a false negative.
cues.zh: 有所謂第二類錯誤，也稱偽陰性。

cues.en: So what does this mean?
cues.zh: 意思是什麼？

cues.en: This means that the test statistic was smaller than our significance threshold.
cues.zh: 檢定統計量小於顯著性門檻。

cues.en: So it was less than the significance threshold.
cues.zh: 低於顯著性門檻。

cues.en: And therefore, we said, well, I'm not going to reject the null hypothesis.
cues.zh: 因此說，不拒絕虛無假設。

cues.en: We don't have enough evidence to reject the null hypothesis in favor of the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 沒有足夠證據拒絕虛無假設、轉而傾向對立假設。

cues.en: However, that's actually the wrong thing to do, because the true state of the world is H naught.
cues.zh: 但其實這樣做錯了，因為真實世界狀態是 H₀。

cues.en: The true state of the world is that the null hypothesis is true.
cues.zh: 真實狀態是虛無假設為真。

cues.en: So we've made a mistake, we just didn't have enough evidence.
cues.zh: 所以犯了錯，只是沒有足夠證據。

cues.en: Really, the true state of the world is that HA is true, but we said that H naught is true.
cues.zh: 真正的真實狀態是 Hₐ 為真，但我們說 H₀ 為真。

cues.en: So that's a mistake, that's called a false negative.
cues.zh: 這是錯誤，稱為偽陰性。

cues.en: Also related to beta statistical power, again, I will talk about that later.
cues.zh: 也和 β、統計檢定力有關，之後會談。

cues.en: For now, you can just focus on the terms, type II error and false negative.
cues.zh: 目前先專注術語：第二類錯誤、偽陰性。

cues.en: Okay, and then, you know, we're gonna go over here next.
cues.zh: 接著看這裡。

cues.en: And this is called a false positive, or a type I error.
cues.zh: 這稱為偽陽性，或第一類錯誤。

cues.en: And this is simply defined by the alpha, which is our significance threshold.
cues.zh: 它直接由 α，也就是顯著性門檻定義。

cues.en: So what a type I error means is that the null hypothesis is actually true.
cues.zh: 第一類錯誤表示，虛無假設其實為真。

cues.en: That's the reality about the world.
cues.zh: 這是真實世界的狀況。

cues.en: The null hypothesis is true, but we happen to get a pretty large test statistic in our sample purely by chance, it can happen.
cues.zh: 虛無假設為真，但純粹偶然，樣本得到很大的檢定統計量，這可能發生。

cues.en: It happens, you know, not all the time, but it happens occasionally.
cues.zh: 不是一直發生，但偶爾會有。

cues.en: So we made a mistake, we said that the null hypothesis isn't true.
cues.zh: 所以犯錯，說虛無假設不成立。

cues.en: We favor the alternative hypothesis, but that was the wrong thing to do, because the reality is that the null hypothesis is really true.
cues.zh: 傾向對立假設，但這樣做不對，因為實際上虛無假設真的為真。

cues.en: So this is a mistake, it's a false positive.
cues.zh: 這是錯誤，是偽陽性。

cues.en: And this other one is a false negative, where we fail to identify a true effect that's really out there in the world.
cues.zh: 另一個是偽陰性，沒有辨識出真實世界中確實存在的效果。

cues.en: Okay, so here you go, all these four colors corresponding to these four boxes in this two by two table.
cues.zh: 這四種顏色，對應二乘二表格中的四個格子。

cues.en: Now, the thing is, you want to avoid these type I and type II errors, but they're kind of difficult to avoid because they're dependent on other factors here.
cues.zh: 想避免第一、第二類錯誤，但不容易，因為還取決於其他因素。

cues.en: So you might say, well, you know, I want to have fewer type I errors.
cues.zh: 你可能說，希望第一類錯誤少一點。

cues.en: I really don't want to have a type I error, I don't want false positives.
cues.zh: 不想犯第一類錯誤，不想有偽陽性。

cues.en: So I'm going to increase my alpha, increase the significance threshold, so that I am less likely to reject the null hypothesis
cues.zh: 所以提高 α、提高顯著性門檻，讓虛無假設為真時，

cues.en: when the null hypothesis is true.
cues.zh: 比較不容易拒絕它。

cues.en: And that is true, you are going to, you know, by increasing alpha, increasing your significant threshold.
cues.zh: 這確實會如此，提高 α、提高顯著性門檻，

cues.en: So this would mean having a P value of 0.01 instead of 0.05.
cues.zh: 也就是 P 值用 0.01，而不是 0.05。

cues.en: So you are reducing the type I errors, that's good, but look what else happens.
cues.zh: 第一類錯誤減少了，很好，但看看還發生什麼。

cues.en: You're like way past the peak of this alternative hypothesis distribution.
cues.zh: 已經遠超過對立假設分布的峰值。

cues.en: So you're reducing the type I errors, that's good, but simultaneously you are also reducing your possibility of having true positives here.
cues.zh: 減少第一類錯誤的同時，也減少了得到真陽性的可能性。

cues.en: So that means you could have real effects out there in the world, in your sample, and you just fail to label them as being real.
cues.zh: 表示真實世界、樣本中可能有真正效果，卻沒有把它標記為真。

cues.en: You get an effect size that's out here, and you're still gonna call that non-significant.
cues.zh: 得到這裡的效果量，仍然會稱為不顯著。

cues.en: You're gonna say, I retain the null hypothesis, even though the true state of the world is that the null hypothesis is wrong.
cues.zh: 保留虛無假設，即使真實世界中，虛無假設是錯的。

cues.en: So this is a problem.
cues.zh: 這是問題。

cues.en: You can't just arbitrarily increase your alpha rate to decrease the false positives.
cues.zh: 不能只是任意提高 α 水準來減少偽陽性。

cues.en: That has implications for reducing the amount of true positives.
cues.zh: 這也會減少真陽性。

cues.en: Okay, and we get the same story over here.
cues.zh: 另一邊也是同樣情況。

cues.en: So you could say, well, you know, I really don't wanna have false negatives, I really don't wanna make any type II errors.
cues.zh: 你可能說，不想有偽陰性，不想犯第二類錯誤。

cues.en: I want to increase my chances of identifying true positives.
cues.zh: 想增加辨識真陽性的機會。

cues.en: When there is really an effect out there in the real world, I want to see it, I want to know that that effect is really there.
cues.zh: 當真實世界真的有效果，希望看見、知道它存在。

cues.en: So then you can reduce your significance threshold, and that's a good thing because it makes your test more sensitive to detecting real effects,
cues.zh: 於是降低顯著性門檻，這很好，因為讓檢定更敏感，能偵測真實效果，

cues.en: if those real effects are present.
cues.zh: 如果效果確實存在。

cues.en: But, obviously, there's gonna be a trade-off here, and the trade-off is that we increase the number of type I errors.
cues.zh: 但顯然會有取捨，就是第一類錯誤增加。

cues.en: So you're more likely to get a test value here, and say that it's a real effect.
cues.zh: 更可能在這裡得到檢定值，說它是真實效果。

cues.en: You claim that your effect is statistically significant, but actually it's really coming from the null hypothesis distribution.
cues.zh: 主張效果統計顯著，但它其實來自虛無假設分布。

cues.en: So again, just increasing or decreasing the significance threshold is not really necessarily a great way to reduce your chances
cues.zh: 所以，只是提高或降低顯著性門檻，不一定是降低

cues.en: of making statistical errors, because there's all these trade-offs that happen in these two distributions.
cues.zh: 統計錯誤機會的好方式，因為兩個分布中存在這些取捨。

cues.en: Okay, before going further, I wanna give you a kind of humorous example of type I and type II errors.
cues.zh: 繼續前，舉個第一、第二類錯誤的幽默例子。

cues.en: I found this on the internet here.
cues.zh: 這是在網路上找到的。

cues.en: I think this is a meme. Is this thing a meme?
cues.zh: 我想是迷因，這算迷因嗎？

cues.en: I'm like slightly too old to be a millennial, I just missed the cutoff for a millennial.
cues.zh: 我稍微比千禧世代年長一點，剛好錯過分界。

cues.en: So I'm a little bit confused about some of these internet terms here.
cues.zh: 所以對某些網路術語有點困惑。

cues.en: So I don't know if this is a meme or a comic.
cues.zh: 不知道這是迷因還是漫畫。

cues.en: This isn't a comic, anyway, it's just a cute thing.
cues.zh: 不是漫畫，總之只是個可愛的東西。

cues.en: Okay, so here is an example of a type I error, which is a false positive.
cues.zh: 這是第一類錯誤，也就是偽陽性的例子。

cues.en: So the true state of the world is the null hypothesis, which is that this man is not pregnant, but the test accidentally revealed evidence for pregnancy.
cues.zh: 真實世界的狀態是虛無假設，也就是這名男子沒有懷孕，但檢測意外顯示懷孕證據。

cues.en: So the doctor has to tell him that he's pregnant, and look how surprised he looks.
cues.zh: 所以醫生必須告訴他懷孕了，看看他多驚訝。

cues.en: Okay, so that's a type I era, false positive.
cues.zh: 這是第一類錯誤、偽陽性。

cues.en: Here's a type II error, this is a false negative.
cues.zh: 這裡是第二類錯誤、偽陰性。

cues.en: So here, the true state of the world is that the alternative hypothesis exists.
cues.zh: 真實世界是對立假設成立。

cues.en: This woman really is pregnant, but the doctor, or the pregnancy test was a mistake.
cues.zh: 這名女子真的懷孕，但醫生或驗孕檢測出了錯。

cues.en: And so the doctor actually tells her, no, no, no, you belong to the null hypothesis group, you belong to the not pregnant group, even though that is inconsistent with the real world.
cues.zh: 因此醫生告訴她，不，你屬於虛無假設組，屬於沒有懷孕的一組，即使這和現實不一致。

cues.en: She really should have rejected the null hypothesis in favor of the alternative hypothesis.
cues.zh: 她其實應該拒絕虛無假設，傾向對立假設。

cues.en: So that's a type II error, also called false negative.
cues.zh: 這是第二類錯誤，也稱偽陰性。

cues.en: Okay, so I showed you two slides ago that it's not really possible to selectively decrease type I errors without affecting your sensitivity,
cues.zh: 前兩張投影片展示過，不可能只減少第一類錯誤，卻不影響敏感度，

cues.en: or only decrease type II errors.
cues.zh: 或者只減少第二類錯誤。

cues.en: But there is a way to generally decrease your possibility of making statistical errors.
cues.zh: 但有一種方式，可以整體降低犯統計錯誤的可能性。

cues.en: And essentially, that works by just trying to minimize the amount of overlap between these distributions, because this is really where the problem comes in.
cues.zh: 基本上，就是盡量減少兩個分布的重疊，因為問題就在這裡。

cues.en: The problem is not here, the problem isn't here, the problem is this amount of overlap here between the null hypothesis distribution and the alternative hypothesis distribution.
cues.zh: 問題不在這裡、也不在那裡，而在虛無假設與對立假設分布的重疊區域。

cues.en: Okay, so we have two ways to minimize our statistical errors in general.
cues.zh: 整體而言，有兩種方式降低統計錯誤。

cues.en: One is to increase the distance between these two distributions, and that basically means just taking these distributions and pushing them further apart from each other.
cues.zh: 一種是增加兩個分布間的距離，把它們推得更遠。

cues.en: Now, the null hypothesis distribution is usually just kind of fixed where it is.
cues.zh: 虛無假設分布通常固定在原來位置。

cues.en: So this is really about moving the alternative hypothesis distribution further to the right or further to the left, depending on which direction it's going in.
cues.zh: 所以其實是把對立假設分布移得更右或更左，取決於方向。

cues.en: But you can see that these two distributions now have a very small overlap.
cues.zh: 可以看到，現在兩個分布重疊很少。

cues.en: So in this case, it's very easy to have a pretty stringent threshold.
cues.zh: 這種情況，很容易使用相當嚴格的門檻。

cues.en: You know, you could have a threshold of maybe 0.001, and that would be out here on the null hypothesis distribution.
cues.zh: 例如 0.001，會落在虛無假設分布這裡。

cues.en: And we still have a lot of power to reject the null hypothesis in favor of the alternative hypothesis, and do that in a accurate and responsible way.
cues.zh: 仍有很大檢定力拒絕虛無假設、傾向對立假設，而且能準確、負責任地這樣做。

cues.en: So how do you do this?
cues.zh: 如何做到？

cues.en: How do you get your distribution to be further away from the null hypothesis distribution?
cues.zh: 怎麼讓分布離虛無假設分布更遠？

cues.en: Well, you know, you just have to look for larger effects.
cues.zh: 就得尋找更大的效果。

cues.en: You have to look for experimental effects that you expect to see, that you expect to be very large, very different from the null hypothesis value.
cues.zh: 尋找預期非常大、和虛無假設值差很多的實驗效果。

cues.en: This would be an example of comparing the heights of giraffes to the heights of slow loris'.
cues.zh: 例如比較長頸鹿和懶猴身高。

cues.en: That's gonna be a huge effect size, very little overlap in those distributions.
cues.zh: 效果量很大，分布重疊很少。

cues.en: Having the distributions be closer together would be, for example, the example I gave of South African giraffes versus North African giraffes.
cues.zh: 分布比較接近的例子，則是先前提的南非與北非長頸鹿。

cues.en: Okay, so this is one way, the other way is to decrease the widths of the distributions.
cues.zh: 這是一種方式，另一種是減少分布寬度。

cues.en: And this means two things.
cues.zh: 這表示兩件事。

cues.en: One, it means having less variability in your data.
cues.zh: 第一，資料變異較少。

cues.en: So the data are closer together...
cues.zh: 資料更靠近。

cues.en: Yeah, there's overall less dispersion in the data, so that tightens up this distribution.
cues.zh: 整體離散程度較低，所以分布縮緊。

cues.en: And the null hypothesis distribution can also be made narrower by changing the degrees of freedom.
cues.zh: 改變自由度，也可以讓虛無假設分布更窄。

cues.en: So the larger your sample size, in general, the narrower these distributions are going to become.
cues.zh: 所以通常樣本數越大，分布越窄。

cues.en: Again, that's related to degrees of freedom, which you learned about in the previous video.
cues.zh: 這同樣和前一部影片學的自由度有關。

cues.en: All right, so that's about type I and type II errors.
cues.zh: 這就是第一、第二類錯誤。

cues.en: I know it can be a little bit confusing when you first encounter these, but these will become more intuitive.
cues.zh: 知道剛接觸時可能有點困惑，但會逐漸更直觀。

cues.en: You'll get more familiar with these as we go through more and more analyses.
cues.zh: 隨著進行越來越多分析，會越來越熟悉。

cues.en: And, of course, as you continue doing statistical analyses on your own in practice.
cues.zh: 當然，自己持續在實務中做統計分析，也會更熟悉。
